blockers.quote: > SCENE: A coaching hall at night under tube lights, rows of desks, a ceiling fan turning. Row three: you, bent over, copying the topper's notebook from the desk beside you, line for line. The thumbnail's set and pose.
blockers.why: story #2: the first seven seconds show copying, not the thumbnail's glowing chip and shocked reaction.
blockers.fix: > SCENE: A coaching hall at night under tube lights. Your crimson chip is already glowing beside your head at 0.04%; you freeze mid-copy, eyes wide, while the topper's notes remain beneath your pen.

suggestions.quote: Last year? About one in a thousand UPSC applicants got in (c01).
suggestions.fix: This is where I would stop watching: the story pauses for a statistic after the stall reversal. Put the fact directly over an action—your chip dropping as you reopen your notebook—and cut lines 89–91's explanation.

suggestions.quote: A year of fees. A year of your life. On one chair. So... keep going?
suggestions.fix: Change “On one chair” to “For one chair” so the sacrifice and question are immediately clear.

keep.quote: One chair. Out of two thousand five hundred.
You can't borrow someone's odds. Only their apron.
The biggest number? It tells you what's likely. It can't tell you what's worth choosing.
